documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

52 yo woman here to establish care. Previous primary office no longer takes her plan. Records requested.

HPI: Type 2 diabetes for several years, on metformin 1000 mg BID, no other agent ever. Also HTN on lisinopril 20 and high cholesterol/triglycerides on atorvastatin 40. Says she used to see an endocrinologist alongside her old PCP, last went in the spring, not planning to go back if we can manage it here. No home glucose meter in use ("the strips ran out"). Takes meds most days. No polyuria, polydipsia, vision change, chest pain, dyspnea, foot sores. Weight has been about the same for years.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, mixed hyperlipidemia, obesity.
PSH: laparoscopic cholecystectomy 2014.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother T2DM. Father HTN and high cholesterol. Maternal grandmother endometrial cancer.
SH: data entry specialist, sits most of the day. Never smoker. No alcohol. No drugs. Lives in Easthampton.
GYN: still having periods, regular. Pap and mammogram done at old office, will confirm from records.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: Vitals as recorded. BMI 35.
Gen: well appearing, pleasant.
HEENT: normal. Neck supple, no thyromegaly.
CV: RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear.
Abd: obese, soft, nontender, healed laparoscopic port scars.
Ext: no edema. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+, monofilament intact bilaterally.
Psych: normal mood and affect.

A/P:
1. T2DM - not at goal by her report. A1c today. Diet basics reviewed. Continue metformin. New meter and strips sent.
2. HTN - above goal today. Continue lisinopril 20, recheck next visit.
3. Mixed hyperlipidemia - continue atorvastatin 40, lipids today.
4. Obesity - talked about walking at lunch.
5. HM - HIV screen today (never done). Records for Pap, colonoscopy, mammogram, vaccines. Flu shot when it arrives.

RTC 4 months, sooner with results.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Ms. Washington,

Your labs from Tuesday are back. Your A1c (3-month sugar average) is above where we want it, and your triglycerides are high. Kidney function, blood counts and the urine protein test look fine, and the HIV screen is negative.

For now: keep taking the metformin twice a day with meals, start using the new meter a few mornings a week, and try to cut back on sweet drinks. We will recheck at your next visit in January.

Your primary care physician

OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 02/24/2022
Re: Tammy Washington, DOB 04/09/1969

Thank you for referring Ms. Washington. She describes about half a year of gradual darkening and thickening of the skin in both underarms and around the neck. No itching or pain. No new medications.

Her diabetes remains poorly controlled on metformin; we reviewed your January labs (A1c 8.5%, fasting glucose 180, total cholesterol 220, LDL 145, HDL 35, triglycerides 250). She also has hypertension. No family history of skin cancer. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BMI 35. Symmetric, hyperpigmented, velvety plaques of both axillae and the neck. No skin tags of concern, no other lesions examined of note.

Fasting insulin drawn today: 32 uIU/mL (high).

Impression: Acanthosis nigricans, consistent with insulin resistance.

Plan: The skin change reflects her insulin resistance and should soften with weight loss and better glucose control. No topical treatment needed at this point. Return as needed.

Dermatology

GASTROENTEROLOGY CONSULT
Visit date: 12/28/2022
Patient: Tammy Washington   DOB 04/09/1969
Referring: primary care

Reason: mild right-sided abdominal discomfort for several weeks, abnormal liver enzymes.

History: 53-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and obesity, seen this year by dermatology for acanthosis nigricans and by sports medicine for knee and foot complaints. The discomfort is mild and intermittent. No nausea, vomiting, weight loss or change in bowel habit. Diabetes and lipids both remain above goal. She takes metformin and a statin; she has not been back to her endocrinologist in more than a year. Cholecystectomy 2014.

Medications (as listed): lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: no tobacco, no alcohol. Sedentary at a desk job, meals at irregular times.

Exam: T 98.4 F, BP 142/90, HR 82, RR 16. BMI 35. Abdomen soft, nontender; liver edge palpable a few cm below the costal margin. No jaundice, palmar erythema, spider angiomata or other signs of chronic liver disease.

Data: AST 52, ALT 63, ALP 90, T bili 0.7 (12/6). A1c 7.9, LDL 158, TG 260. Hepatitis B surface antigen negative and hepatitis C antibody nonreactive today.

Impression: Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, diagnosed clinically: mild hepatomegaly and transaminase elevation in the setting of diabetes, obesity and hypertriglyceridemia, viral hepatitis excluded, no alcohol.

Recommendations:
1. Weight loss of 7 to 10 percent of body weight is the treatment with the best evidence. Regular activity, fewer refined carbohydrates.
2. Continue her statin; it is safe in fatty liver disease.
3. Better diabetes control per primary care.
4. Repeat liver tests with her routine labs. GI follow-up as needed.

Gastroenterology

GI follow-up - 04/26/2024
Re: Tammy Washington (DOB 04/09/1969)

Ms. Washington returns, last seen here in December 2022 for right upper quadrant discomfort and NASH. For about six months she has had fatigue and the RUQ ache again. No alcohol. Medications include metformin and lisinopril; listed: atorvastatin 40 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: BMI 32 (down from 35). Liver enlarged on palpation. No jaundice, ascites or spider angiomata.

Ultrasound today: hepatic steatosis; post-cholecystectomy; no ductal dilatation.

Assessment: NASH, transaminases higher than 2022 despite some weight loss. Synthetic function and platelets preserved.

Plan: MRI of the abdomen with and without contrast to better characterize the liver. Continue weight loss efforts. Will forward results.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: GI follow-up note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: GI note 4/26 reviewed: AST 70, ALT 85, bili 1.2, albumin 4.0, plt 220; US steatosis, no ductal dilatation. GI ordering MRI abdomen. Pt aware, MRI booked 5/20 per her. Will watch for report.

reports.study: MRI abdomen with and without contrast
reports.text: MRI abdomen without and with IV hepatobiliary contrast. Liver enlarged with diffuse signal loss on opposed-phase imaging, consistent with steatosis. A single 2.6 cm well-circumscribed lesion in hepatic segment 6 shows arterial phase enhancement without washout and is hypointense on the hepatobiliary phase, features of hepatocellular adenoma. No other hepatic lesion. Portal and hepatic veins patent. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation. Gallbladder surgically absent. Spleen normal in size. Pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys unremarkable. No ascites or lymphadenopathy.
reports.conclusion: 1. Single 2.6 cm segment 6 lesion consistent with hepatocellular adenoma. 2. Hepatic steatosis.

documents.title: Your MRI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Tammy, I have your MRI report and the GI note. Besides the fatty liver, the MRI found a single small growth in the liver, 2.6 cm, that looks like a hepatic adenoma. That's a benign (non-cancer) growth of liver cells. The usual plan for one this size is what GI recommends: avoid estrogen (your IUD is a progestin, not estrogen, so it's fine), keep losing weight, and repeat the MRI in about a year to make sure it stays the same. GI will order that.

I know "growth in the liver" sounds scary. Happy to talk it through on the phone or at your physical.
